Why this matters for your business: If you build products on top of someone else's AI models, you inherit their pricing, their reliability and their release schedule. If the report is accurate, it is a cautionary tale for every business planning AI features: own the parts that matter, and price the rest properly from day one.
The number that stands out: A reported one-third cut to the 2026 revenue forecast, unconfirmed by Canva.
Cut through the AI noise. Get the weekly brief for business: 
#AIinBusiness #AIBusinessStrategy #SaaS
Source: The Verge, 7 August 2026 [...] The winners of this AI cycle are not the companies with the flashiest demos. They are the ones who fix unit economics first. Own the models, or charge for the compute honestly.
Canva will survive this. Most startups copying the 'add AI to everything' playbook will not.
#AI #SaaS #Startups #BusinessStrategy
August 9, 2026 | Source: Startup Daily / The Verge [...] Canva just told investors to expect less growth, and the reason should worry every SaaS founder.
The design giant cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20%. Q2 revenue hit $921.9M, up 25% year on year, but it still missed guidance. Some AI features are running six months late.
The cost: serving AI on someone else's frontier models. Every magic resize, every AI image edit, every 'generate' burns tokens billed by OpenAI and friends. Canva's own models were not ready, so it rented intelligence at frontier prices.
CEO Melanie Perkins calls it a deliberate decision to get the economics right. Translation: free AI features were never free. They are a pricing trap that lands on the P&L one quarter later.

The team’s production studio has created more than 50 films for companies including Cognition, Physical Intelligence, and Gumloop. This gave them the experience to spot where AI could aid in the creative process.

We spent our first seven months as a film studio, creating 50+ films for companies like Cognition, First Round, and Andera. Then we turned everything we learned into software. Today, teams at Webflow, Resend, Rho, and Gumloop use Osmo to ship video 32.7x faster than After Effects, without giving up creative control.
We're also announcing our $5M seed led by Bain Capital Ventures, with participation from Basis Set Ventures, MVP Ventures, Collaborative Fund, Scott Belsky, and others. Grateful to be backed by people who believe taste belongs to humans.

Import a Figma file, paste in frontend code, or drop in a reference video. It generates animation as editable code, with control over the timeline, layers, vectors, motion, and brand rules. results.title: Osmo Studio: End-to-End Editable Video Platform for Storytellers | Chris He posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content:
It has been a joy to think deeply about verifiable vs unverifiable rewards, continually improving agent harnesses, multimodal reasoning, efficiency, and the form factor of software with ai and human consumers in mind. Very grateful to our investors Bain Capital Ventures (BCV), Basis Set, Collaborative Fund, MVP Ventures, Scott Belsky, Sarah Smith, Kevin Patrick Mahaffey, and many others for our $5M seed.
I am so continuously inspired by the relentless eye for detail, joy, and craft of our team Oleksandr Shevenionov Basil Alfaro Will Hoppin Chris He Sophie Salvadori-Roam Sam Grozian Pedro Marnoto Pereira Nikolas Welchel Justine Chang. The most personal is truly the most creative!
Check us out at osmo.inc [...] We at Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) with Amanda Huang are delighted to be leading the $5m seed of Osmo Studio. Chris He, Will Hoppin, Oleksandr Shevenionov, and Basil Alfaro have a rare combination: creative geniuses and technologists. They tell stories that break through.
You've seen the videos they've made on your feeds for Cog, PI and Parallel Web Systems. I was struck by their level of intensity and passion for filmmaking. It shows in the product. [...] Our team is full of directors, cinematographers, and editors who spent their careers on real sets including at A24, NBC and Saturday Night Live. We’ve made 50+ films in the last 7 months for Cognition, Parallel Web Systems, Physical Intelligence, Basis, and some of the fastest-growing companies alive, all on the exact tool we're releasing today.
Thank you to our earliest believers, who put $5M behind our mission - Hollywood and Silicon Valley under one roof, and tools that empower the next generation of storytellers to express themselves freely. Led by Bain Capital Ventures (BCV), with Basis Set, MVP Ventures, Collaborative Fund, Sarah Smith Fund, Scott Belsky, Kevin Patrick Mahaffey and others.
